svg.title: Slonczewski CPP/MTJ torque vs Zhang-Li CIP gradient torque in Fullmag
svg.desc: Panel (a) shows SlonczewskiSTT CPP/MTJ trilayer geometry, angular asymmetry parameter Lambda, and computed angular efficiency curves epsilon_DL(theta). Panel (b) shows ZhangLiSTT CIP domain-wall translation, separating conventional current J_c from electron drift, spin-drift velocity u, and adiabatic vs non-adiabatic torques. The bottom strip states the single Gilbert-to-explicit RHS conversion invariant.
svg.text: Spin-Transfer Torque: Slonczewski CPP/MTJ vs Zhang–Li CIP Domain-Wall Models
Conventional charge current J_c (e > 0) drives both local realizations; Gilbert source T_G converts to explicit RHS exactly once
(Legacy v0 uses 2 e M_s t_F & fixed_layer_position)
Relative angle θ between m and p̂
TSLG​ = ΩJ​ ε_DL(m) [m × (m × p̂)] + ΩJ​ ε′ (m × p̂)
• Thin-layer homogenized (slonczewski_thin_layer_homogenized.v1): executable on FDM & FEM.
• Interface flux (slonczewski_interface_flux.v1): authoring/IR only (fail-closed on FDM & FEM).
• Mutually exclusive drive: prescribed current_density OR named current_source.
• Canonical v2 requires id, target, stack_normal, free_layer_thickness_m (no silent fallback).
• Notice: slonczewski.fullmag.v2 flips m×(m×p̂) = −m×(p̂×m); check sign with stack_normal.
• Zero DL torque when m ∥ ±p̂; odd scaling under J_⊥ sign reversal.
CIP domain-wall motion (computed Néel/Bloch profile m(x))
Canonical equations never switch to electron-flow signs mid-formula; sign is fixed to conventional Jc​ & e > 0.
Zhang–Li velocity, Gilbert form, and FDM vs FEM formulas
u = [g μB​ P / (2 e Ms​)] Jc​ | TZLG​ = −(u·∇)m + β m × [(u·∇)m]
• FEM canonical (zhang_li.fullmag.v1): P1 tetrahedral ∇m, user lande_g, exact e.
• FDM MuMax3-compat (zhang_li.mumax3.v1): central clamped stencil, fixed g = 2.0, (1+β²)⁻¹.
• Legacy (zhang_li.legacy_fullmag.v0): retained for migration; never silently upgraded.
• Supports prescribed current_density OR named current_source (mutually exclusive).
• Aliases: xi maps to beta (contradictory nonzero values fail validation).
• Active planner gate: currently one executable spin-torque module at a time.
Texplicit​ = (TG​ + α m × TG​) / (1 + α²) [applied EXACTLY ONCE before RHS integration]
Backends must NEVER pre-convert T_G to explicit form and then convert it a second time in the LLG layer; transport observations retain unconverted T_G.
